title: Hosted SSE: late-chunk attribution and client reconciliation protocol
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported corrupted or truncated streaming responses from the Hosted API during midstream interruptions. Symptoms include: client-visible duplicate tokens, missing trailing punctuation, or entire final fragments never delivered despite server-side completion. Root cause analysis shows race conditions between the connection handoff/resume path and the server chunk flush logic when a reconnect occurs within a short window (10s) of the original stream closing. This ticket defines a reconciliation protocol and an implementation plan to ensure deterministic attribution of late-arriving chunks and a safe, idempotent resume handshake for clients.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running streaming generation (>= 20s) against hosted.redwood.example/generate with SSE streaming enabled and idempotency-key header. 2) Forcefully drop the client socket around token boundary (e.g., SIGINT). 3) Immediately reconnect using a resume-token returned in the last event or an idempotency-key-based resume API. 4) Observe duplicated suffix tokens or missing final punctuation in client-assembled stream when server had flushed the same tokens to an out-of-band buffer during disconnect handling.
recent_customer_reports: Customer A (Fintech) — production user-facing truncation causing failed compliance logs, escalated Feb 18.
Customer B (SaaS) — duplicate last-word tokens during reconnects over flaky mobile networks, escalated Feb 20.
Customer C (Healthcare) — observed final JSON chunk never delivered, causing downstream parse errors, reported Feb 21.
observed_behavior: When a client reconnects quickly, the proxy path can create a fresh session that races with the server flush-to-buffer operation. The server may have already committed final tokens to persistent metrics/logs and a short-lived out-of-band retention buffer, while the live stream connection got closed before emitting final event framing. Clients that naively stitch events by ordering arrival time end up with duplicates or missing fragments depending on which stream win the race.
root_cause_summary: 1) Missing durable per-request sequence namespace for chunks across reconnects. 2) Resume handshake only included a timestamp; no monotonic sequence or checksum to detect overlapping fragments. 3) Server flush and retention logic does not mark chunk ownership consistently when a concurrent new session is created for the same request id. 4) Client-side reassembly logic assumes strictly increasing arrival order and single-source origin.
proposed_solution_overview: Introduce a light-weight reconciliation protocol: (A) Every stream chunk will carry a stream_seq (monotonic integer) and chunk_hash (short checksum) in the SSE event meta. (B) On reconnect the server issues a resume-token that encodes last-ack-seq and a short retention handle; clients supply that token to request only the missing seq range. (C) Server keeps a soft retention buffer for completed streams for 60s keyed by request-id + resume-handle to allow safe backfill of late chunks. (D) Make server-side chunk emit idempotent by checking seq/hash and discarding duplicates. (E) Roll out feature behind a runtime feature flag and opt-in header to limit blast radius.
implementation_details: - API changes: SSE event format adds headers: 'x-rw-stream-seq', 'x-rw-chunk-hash'. Resume flow: POST /v1/streams/resume with resume-token -> returns missing seqs or 'ok' if none. - Server: extend stream writer to assign seq numbers atomically, compute 32-bit FNV hash over chunk payload, and persist (seq,hash,payload) to a 60s in-memory LRU buffer (sharded per pod). - Proxy: when creating a new session for a resume request, validate incoming resume-token matches last-known request-id and replay only missing seqs. - Client SDK: add automatic resume handshake, prefer resume-token when reconnecting within retention window, and on merge check chunk_hash mismatch to flag integrity errors to the app. - Backwards compatibility: if 'x-rw-stream-seq' absent treat as legacy stream; servers with flag disabled keep existing behavior.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for seq assignment and duplicate discard logic. - Integration test: simulated flappy network where client reconnects with resume-token; assert no duplicates, no missing final punctuation across 10k randomized runs. - Chaos test: k8s pod kill during final chunk emission and immediate client reconnects. - Fuzz: random chunk truncation + resume handshake mismatch to ensure clients surface integrity errors. - Customers in beta: opt-in list (Customer A,B) to validate real traffic patterns before full rollout.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: 'rw.streams.resume_attempts', 'rw.streams.backfill_served', 'rw.streams.duplicate_chunks_discarded', 'rw.streams.checksum_mismatch'. Dashboards: per-model and per-region charts for resume_attempts vs backfill_served, SLA delta for stream-latency tail p99 before and after. Alerts: fire when duplicate_chunks_discarded rate > 0.1% of resume_attempts for 5m or when checksum_mismatch > 0 for >1m (customer-facing integrity issue).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement server buffer + seq/hash logic behind feature flag (runtime:stream_reconcile). 2) Ship client SDK changes to beta channel (js/python-go). 3) Enable feature for internal infra traffic and run 48h canary. 4) Invite Customer A and B to opt-in beta with a support runbook. 5) If stable, gradually enable on hosted infra by region over 72h. 6) Deprecation: keep legacy path for 90 days; after full enable, emit deprecation warning header to old clients.
customer_communication: - Immediate: provide Customer A/B/C nightly interim mitigation (server-side forced final-flush and explicit resume-token in responses). - Postfix: detailed postmortem to impacted customers describing root cause, fix design, and timeline. - SDK: release notes and migration guide showing how to enable resume-token and handle checksum errors.
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chosen seq+checksum resume approach over full durable replays to minimize storage and latency (Decision by Diego, Priya, Sam).
2026-03-02: Opted for 60s retention window; balances common reconnect windows and memory cost (Ops sign-off).
2026-03-05: Feature will be behind runtime flag with opt-in header for safe canarying.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: additional per-chunk metadata increases event size; mitigate by using compact seq (32-bit) and 32-bit hash. Risk: retention buffer memory growth in high-concurrency tenants; mitigate with per-tenant quota and early-drop with logged rationale. Risk: buggy client SDK integration could mis-handle resume token; provide strict validation and fallback to legacy fetch if integrity fails.
open_questions: Should we expose resume-token semantics in public API docs immediately or keep behind beta?
Is 60s retention sufficient for customers on poor mobile networks with minutes-long reconnect windows?
Do enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments get a config knob for retention window size?
